title: A cyclone-count heat buffer was not clear in six ocean-period coral survey samples from 1998 to 2019
abstract: We tested whether a long-term cyclone count marked a weaker coral bleaching response to heat. We used 6,217 repeated Reef Check site-month records at 1,411 sites in three oceans in 1998-2019. The model controlled for site, ocean-year, ocean-month, and depth. Per 25 units of the interpolated 1964-2014 cyclone count, the pooled heat slope changed by +5.13 bleaching percentage points per four degree-heating weeks. The nominal 95% interval was -8.76 to +19.02. No ocean-period cell had a clear negative interval after correction for six tests. The early Atlantic cell had a positive interval. Same-calendar-month controls gave -11.36, with an interval of -25.89 to +3.16. These results do not establish an absence of storm cooling. The site count is not an event measure, heat can mediate cooling, and survey selection and coral composition remain uncontrolled. The package includes the audited panel, source hash, code, checks, and figures.

display.caption: Cyclone-count interaction estimates across ocean-period samples and pooled sensitivity checks. Negative values fit a heat buffer. Left intervals correct for six tests; right intervals are nominal 95%.

citations.reason: The event cooling mechanism motivates a distinct test of a long-term site indicator.
